item.title: A relative version of Weinstein's morphism
item.description: arXiv:2611.01083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a relative version of Weinstein's morphism associated to a Lagrangian submanifold \(L\) of a closed symplectic manifold \((M,\omega)\). We construct a homomorphism \[ \mathcal{A}^{(L,\alpha)}\colon \pi_{1}\bigl(\operatorname{Ham}_0(M,L)\bigr) \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}/\mathcal{P}_{2}(M,\omega), \] and establish its basic properties. We compute the invariant in several examples, including latitude circles in \(S^2\), and more generally, Lagrangian fibers in toric manifolds. These computations provide obstructions to Ha\-mil\-to\-nian isotopy of Lagrangian submanifolds and detect nontrivial, and in some cases infinite-order, elements in the homotopy groups of their Hamiltonian stabilizers.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'es Pedroza, Daniel Villanueva-Vega

item.title: Nearby Lagrangians in the cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle
item.description: arXiv:2611.01506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the nearby Lagrangian conjecture for the Klein bottle: every closed connected embedded exact Lagrangian submanifold of its cotangent bundle is Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section by a compactly supported isotopy. The proof passes to the torus double cover and builds on the theorem of Dimitroglou Rizell, Goodman, and Ivrii for the two-dimensional torus. The main step is to construct an isotopy compatible with the covering involution. We achieve this using holomorphic sphere rulings in $S^2\times S^2$ adapted to the zero section, allowing the construction to descend to the Klein bottle.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Gao, Weiwei Wu, Tianyu Yuan

item.title: Partially wrapped contact Fukaya categories of 1-jet spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category of a 1-jet space equipped with a stop, which is an \(A_\infty\)-category of Legendrians equipped with representations of their Chekanov-Eliashberg algebras. This category is invariant under contact isotopies of the stop. We prove a wrapping exact triangle and a generation theorem. When the stop is bounded subanalytic singular isotropic, we prove a Morita equivalence between the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category and a microlocal sheaf category.
item.dc:creator: Hanming Liu

item.title: Fiber-Connectivity of Almost-Toric Systems in Four-Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.02165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the fiber connectivity of proper almost-toric systems $\Phi$ on connected four-dimensional symplectic manifolds. Using Morse--Kirwan theory, we establish three sufficient conditions for fiber connectivity. These results generalize and extend the fiber connectivity results of Pelayo, Ratiu, and Vu Ngoc (2015) by relaxing some of their hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Aerim Si

item.title: Topological triviality of exact Lagrangian Cobordisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.03041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by the rigidity of exact Lagrangian submanifolds, a conjecture by P.~Biran and O.~Cornea asks if a simple exact Lagrangian cobordism $W$ in a tame exact symplectic manifold is always ``symplectically trivial'' (i.e. the Lagrangian suspension of an Hamiltonian isotopy). In this short note, we prove a topological version of this conjecture~: if the cobordism has dimension at least $6$, it is always topologically trivial. This extends a previous work of Lara Suarez who reduced the question to proving an injectivity result among fundamental groups.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Barraud

item.title: Decomposable concordances induce closed immersions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a decomposable Lagrangian concordance between two Legendrian links must induce a closed immersion between the sheaf moduli of its ends. As the main application of this criterion, we prove a conjecture of Cornwell-Ng-Sivek, showing that their Lagrangian concordance is not decomposable. This establishes the first known example of a regular Lagrangian concordance between Legendrian knots that is not decomposable. In addition, we show that even the simpler Lagrangian concordance, satelliting via the Reeb 2-copy, is not decomposable.
item.dc:creator: Roger Casals

item.title: There is only one transitive Anosov flow (in dimension 3, with orientable foliations, up to bicontact padding and Goodman surgeries)
item.description: arXiv:2611.00977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a new surgical operation on Anosov flows, which we call bicontact padding surgery. The operation is defined using the machinery of strongly adapted bicontact structures, and involves inserting a 'padding' layer where one of the contact structures rotates many times around the Reeb flow of the other. We show that every skew Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a finite cover of a geodesic flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. Together with previous results, this implies that every transitive Anosov flow with orientable stable and unstable foliations can be transformed into a suspension flow using bicontact padding surgery and Goodman surgery. This gives some progress towards the Christy-Fried-Ghys conjecture, which predicts that the same statement is true using only Goodman surgery.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Barthelm\'e, Federico Salmoiraghi, Chi Cheuk Tsang

item.title: Braided Multisections and Aspherical Stein Fillings
item.description: arXiv:2611.01833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct Stein fillings diffeomorphic to complements of a connected symplectic unbranched multisection and a regular sphere fiber in the ruled surface $\Sigma_g\times S^2$. For every $g\geq2$ and every multisection degree $p\geq4$, a fixed contact three-manifold admits infinitely many pairwise nonhomeomorphic aspherical fillings of this form. Their first and second integral homology groups are $\Z^{2g}\oplus\Z/p$ and $\Z^{(2g-1)(p-1)}$, respectively, and their intersection pairings vanish. We vary the braid monodromy while preserving the marked contact boundary. Unbounded torsion orders in the first homology of regular unbranched covers of degree $p2^{p-1}$ detect infinitely many isomorphism types of fundamental groups. We also give an equivariant Weinstein handle construction for the cyclic filling $W_{g,4}$. The contact boundaries are supported by spinal open books with planar pages and have positive ordinary support genus.
item.dc:creator: Anar Akhmedov

item.title: Isometric Embeddings of Hyperk\"{a}hler $\mathrm{T}^*\mathbb{CP}^{n}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02089v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct explicit $U(n)$-equivariant isometric embeddings $T^*\mathbb{CP}^{n-1} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^{n^4+2n^2-1}$, $n\ge 2$, with respect to Calabi's hyperk\"{a}hler metric on $T^*\mathbb{CP}^{n-1}$. To achieve this, we first construct a diffeomorphism from $T^*\mathbb{CP}^{n-1}$ onto the manifold of rank-1 projections in $M_n(\mathbb{C})$, such that the pullback of half of the trace-class norm is a K\"{a}hler potential for the hyperk\"{a}hler metric. We then use the Hilbert space structure of $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ to produce the isometric embeddings into Euclidean space.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Lackman

item.title: Universal Curve Counting in Calabi-Yau 4-folds
item.description: arXiv:2611.02717v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, Pardon introduced a universal curve counting framework, which allows him to show that curve counting on 3-folds is "generated" by local curves (in a precise sense). We implement this universal curve counting program for Calabi-Yau 4-folds, where a significant technical difficulty comes from the dependence of the virtual dimension on the genus, which leads to more complicated generators than just local curves. Our main techniques are combinations of deformation-theoretic and homotopy-theoretic methods with an adaptation of Pardon's generic transversality results, which allow us to establish a full set of (computable) generators for CY4 curve counting. As a result, we prove (a slight correction of) the Gromov-Witten/Pandharipande-Thomas correspondence with primary descendents for CY4-folds, formulated by Cao, Maulik, and Toda. From this, we additionally obtain integrality of Gopakumar-Vafa style invariants for CY4-folds, as conjectured by Klemm-Pandharipande.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Karpov, Felix Thimm

item.title: Quasimorphisms and bounded cohomology of transformation groups of nonorientable surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.02847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $N_g$ be a closed connected nonorientable surface of genus $g\ge1$, let $\omega$ be a smooth positive density, and let $\mu$ be a good measure. In this paper we generalize the Gambaudo--Ghys construction using homogeneous quasimorphisms on the central quotients of the braid groups of $N_g$. We prove injectivity of this map for density-preserving diffeomorphisms. For $g\ge2$ and quasimorphisms vanishing on the disc braid group, we obtain an injective map to $C^0$-continuous homogeneous quasimorphisms on $Homeo_0(N_g,\mu)$. We also obtain undistortion criteria in $Homeo_0(N_g)$ and $Diff_0(N_g)$. For $g=1,2$ and every $d\ge2$, we prove $$ \dim\overline H_b^d(Homeo_0(N_g,\mu))=\infty,\qquad \dim\overline{EH}_b^d(Diff_0(N_g,\omega))=\infty. $$ Moreover, $\overline{EH}_b^d(Homeo_0(N_2,\mu))$ is infinite dimensional in every positive even degree $d$. Here $\overline{H}_b^d$ and $\overline{EH}_b^d$ denote reduced bounded cohomology and reduced exact bounded cohomology, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Michael Brandenbursky

item.title: Magnetic cotangent groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2606.22288v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce magnetic cotangent groupoids on the cotangent bundle of a Lie groupoid using normalized cocycles, and characterize when magnetic symplectic forms are multiplicative on these groupoids. We show that $\mathbb{S}^1$-central extensions of Lie groupoids yield such structures via symplectic reduction. For a Kac--Moody extension, the resulting deformation connects the coadjoint and gauge action groupoids, which are not Morita equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Dadi Ni, Kaichuan Qi

item.title: Multiplicity of brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.29917v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove multiplicity results for geometrically distinct brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization $S^1$-bundles under geometric and dynamical assumptions. The lower bounds are expressed in terms of the sum of the mod-two Betti numbers of the real locus of the base. Our proofs combine Lagrangian Rabinowitz Floer homology with the index iteration theory for brake orbits. As an application, we obtain a sharp lower bound for the number of brake geodesics on Finsler spheres with pinched flag curvature.
item.dc:creator: Peng Liu, Dong Xie

item.title: Family Seiberg-Witten equation on Kahler surface and $\pi_i(\Symp)$ on multiple-point blow ups of Calabi-Yau surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2412.19375v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\omega$ be a Kahler form on $M$, which is a torus $T^4$, a $K3$ surface or an Enriques surface, let $M\#n\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ be $n-$point Kahler blowup of $M$. Suppose that $\kappa=[\omega]$ satisfies certain irrationality condition. Applying techniques related to deformation of complex objects, we extend the guage-theoretic invariant on closed Kahler suraces developed by Kronheimer\cite{Kronheimer1998} and Smirnov\cite{Smirnov2022}\cite{Smirnov2023}. As a result, we show that even dimensional higher homotopy groups of $\Symp(M\#n\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2},\omega)$ are infinitely generated.
item.dc:creator: Yi Du

item.title: Holomorphic disks with boundary on compact Lagrangian surface
item.description: arXiv:2505.19407v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $L$ be a compact oriented Lagrangian surface in a K\"ahler surface endowed with a complete Riemannian metric (compatible with the symplectic structure and the complex structure) with bounded sectional curvatures and a positive lower bound on injectivity radius. We show that for every nontrivial class $[\gamma]$ of the fundamental group $\pi_1(L)$ such that $\gamma$ bounds a topological disk in $M$, there exists a holomorphic disk whose boundary belongs to $L$ and is freely homotopic to $\gamma$ on $L$. This answers a question of Bennequin on existence of $J$-holomorphic disks. Nonexistence of exact Lagrangian embeddings of certain surfaces is established in such K\"ahler surface if the fundamental form is exact. In the almost K\"ahler setting, especially, the cotangent bundles of compact manifolds, results on nonexistence of $J$-holomorphic disks and existence of minimizers of the partial energies in the sense of A. Lichnerowicz are obtained.
item.dc:creator: Jingyi Chen

item.title: Twisted scalar curvature as a moment map
item.description: arXiv:2601.18141v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop the moment map theory of the twisted scalar curvature of a K\"ahler metric. Primarily, we introduce a coupled system of equations on a holomorphic submersion intertwining the twisted scalar curvature of a K\"ahler metric on the base and the fibrewise scalar curvature of a relatively K\"ahler metric on the total space. This resulting system can be viewed as producing the natural coupled metric geometry of holomorphic submersions, and we show that this system appears canonically as a moment map. The approach generalises to foliations, where we prove similar results.
item.dc:creator: Ruadha\'i Dervan, Thomas Murphy, Julius Ross, Lars Martin Sektnan, Xiaowei Wang

item.title: Leafrians, Frobenius splittings, and moduli spaces over Poisson surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31619v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Poisson surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, and let $s\in H^0(X,\omega_X^{-1})$ be nonzero. We construct an anticanonical section associated to $s$, called the leafrian, on moduli spaces $M$ of stable objects on $X$, including the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons. The leafrian splits $M$ if and only if $s^{p-1}$ Frobenius splits the base. It is invariant under the Hamiltonian flows of Bottacin's Poisson structure on $M$, so every compatibly split subvariety of $M$ is a Poisson subvariety. Furthermore, the leafrian extends to an anticanonical section on the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$, and splits $\bar M$ under the same criterion. As a consequence, in characteristic zero, for $X$ a smooth projective Poisson surface with a smooth or empty anticanonical divisor and $\rho>0$ (positive leaf rank), the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$ satisfies Kodaira-type cohomology vanishing, including singular $\bar M$.
item.dc:creator: Jun Peng

item.title: Abelianization and moment maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.42123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When $X_G=\mathbb{C}^n/\!/G$ is a GIT quotient of a vector space, replacing $G$ with a maximal torus $T \subset G$ produces a closely related toric variety $X_T:=\mathbb{C}^N/\!/T$, the \emph{Abelianization} of $X_G$. Abelian/non-Abelian correspondences connect structures on $X_G$ with structures on $X_T$. In this paper, we study the interaction between the toric moment map $\mu$ of $X_T$ and $X_G$, when $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$. We do this by looking at the restriction of $\mu$ to an intermediate space $Z/T \subset X_T$, where $Z/G=X_G$. We show that the generic fibres of this map are co-Lagrangians that project to Lagrangians on $X_G$. We completely describe the image in the case where $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(2,n)$, and show that in the general $\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$ case the image can be sliced so that each piece is determined by a finite set of points, related to matroid circuits.
item.dc:creator: Elana Kalashnikov, Ruxandra Moraru, Francisco Villacis
